Token section interpretation: T_total−TTFT excludes the TTFT portion, which the article says includes queue, yet it says lower throughput with unchanged model latency points to queue·network overhead. Queue time is not in this throughput denominator, so the causal claim looks doubtful.

Sampling formula assumption: “이 식은 균일 sampling의 하한 추정치” is ambiguous. Under its independence assumption the formula is the exact miss probability for uniform sampling, and mixing in tail sampling would make it an upper bound on misses.

Convergence §6 '왜 R/γ의 제곱이 나오는가': the step to Mγ ≤ R√M silently assumes that the weights start at 0 and are updated only on mistakes, where y·wᵀx ≤ 0. That condition is what bounds ‖w‖² ≤ MR². The text does not state either assumption.

TwoLevelScheduling §'이 사슬 구조 때문에 tokenizer가 맞지 않으면' and the CalculationWalkthrough say the selector cannot find the cached pod (expected hit 0) when its tokenizer differs from the engine's. If the selector writes its index and hashes new requests with the same tokenizer of its own, its index lookups still match each other. The mismatch would then make the selector's prediction disagree with the engine's real cache rather than drop it to 0, unless the index is filled from engine-side token IDs. My Viz shows only the chain mechanism, a request that differs at token 10, and does not repeat the tokenizer claim.

LinearSoftmax label smoothing: the 'idea' text says the remaining probability is split evenly over 'the other K-1 tokens'. The formula q'(k)=(1-ε)·1[k=y*]+ε/K gives ε/K to all K tokens, including the correct one, so the prose and the formula disagree slightly.

§7 / bridge text / ReviewPrompt 1: the article uses M_peak = max_t Σ live(t), and §3–4 assume input and output are held together during the transform (4.25GiB). By that formula, freeing the input table before hashing lowers the hash-moment sum to ≈2.75GiB, but the peak becomes the transform moment at 4.25GiB, not 2.75GiB. So the bridge sentence '동시 유지와 먼저 해제의 2GiB 차이' and the phrase '약 2.75GiB로 내려갑니다' read as a 2GiB drop in peak, when the peak by the article's own formula drops only 0.5GiB (4.75→4.25). The only exception is an in-place transform. The Viz shows the hash-moment sum as 2.75 and marks ③ 4.25GiB as the peak in that scenario.

Scene 1's own note says these bytes are ones "host가 쓰고 바꿀 수 있으므로". Checking in shared memory and then copying leaves a double-fetch (TOCTOU) window: the host can change the bytes after the check and before the copy. The safe order is to copy into private memory first and validate the private copy. Fixing this needs both a prose change and an outside security fact, so I left it for the author.

MerkleFoldViz calls 23 'leaf의 tree 안 위치 번호 (Helios 코드의 index 23)'. The article prose says siblings fold 'generalized index 방향에 따라'. Per the consensus spec, 23 is the generalized index with the leading 1 bit removed (Electra gindex 87 = 64 + 23), not the generalized index itself. The Viz never calls 23 the generalized index, so it is not wrong. Spelling out that link would need an outside spec fact (87) that the article does not state, so I left it.

Checked against codebase/helios-0.11.1 and found correct: proof.rs gives next committee (23, 6) for Electra and finality depth 7. 23 is 010111 in binary, so the bits read from the low end are 1,1,1,0,1,0. A bit of 1 puts the sibling first (hasher.update(node) before derived_root). In verify.rs the gate order matches the seven gates. The store parameter is &LightClientStore, and the function returns Ok(()). The participation example has 6 of 8 bits set, matching 'key 6개'.
